targetAudience.primary: Engineers evaluating failure recovery and automated repair in agent runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands traces, retries, tool calls and nondeterministic execution.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A full rerun succeeds, but too many variables changed to show that the proposed fix addressed the original failure.

whyNow: A primary study over 536 confirmed failures across three multi-agent frameworks reports higher same-failure reproduction with controlled replay and much higher repair from symptom-driven intervention than from unguided rerun.

externalHook.description: Freeze a represented failed prefix, fail closed on divergence, intervene at an explicit anchor, and regenerate only the suffix.

coreProposition: A causal repair claim requires an authoritative failed logical prefix, fail-closed divergence detection, an explicit intervention anchor, and independent qualification of external state needed by the live suffix; rerun success alone is resampling evidence, not proof of repair.

originalValue.description: Separates logical-prefix fidelity from external-state validity and gives rerun, replay and repair different evidence semantics.

readerTakeaway: Treat recovery experiments as versioned test fixtures; require both prefix fidelity and external-state qualification before interpreting suffix success as causal repair.

supported: The study reports controlled replay reproducing the same failure more often than unguided rerun under tested protocols.
Unguided rerun repairs 6.90% at pass@3 while symptom-driven single-attempt intervention repairs 20.15%.
The replay mechanism validates position/request alignment and stops on divergence.
Reported exactness is limited to represented captured state.
uncertain: The sufficient external-state contract for each tool class
Canonicalization that ignores harmless differences without accepting material divergence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The conclusion is a general recovery-verification pattern for agent runtimes.

decisionReason: The benchmark and explicit replay limitations support a concrete causal-test design with bounded validity claims.
